title: Into the Darkness
text: Why do some of the strangest animals in the ocean grow so enormous in the one place that seems to have almost nothing to eat?

title: Into the Darkness
text: Imagine sinking below the waves into a darkness so complete that no amount of waiting will ever let your eyes adjust.
nxt: Miles of cold water press down on every side.

title: Into the Darkness
text: What is going on in the deep sea, and why does life there so often become gigantic?

title: Deep-Sea Gigantism
text: Common sense says such a place should only support tiny life.
nxt: No sunlight means no plants, and no plants means food must be scarce.

title: Deep-Sea Gigantism
text: But when submersible lights shine into the abyss, they do not just find microscopic drift.
nxt: Many creatures down here have expanded into breathtaking titans.

title: Deep-Sea Gigantism
text: Science calls this deep-sea gigantism, or abyssal gigantism.
nxt: It is the tendency of certain marine species to grow far larger than their shallow-water relatives.

title: The Giant Isopod
text: Before we look for the reason, let us meet the animals. Start with the giant isopod.

title: The Giant Isopod
text: If you lift a damp flowerpot in your garden, you will probably find a pillbug,
nxt: barely the size of a fingernail, curling into a ball when touched.

nxt: In the deep ocean, the giant isopod crawls over the muddy seafloor and grows up to about forty centimeters long.

title: The Giant Isopod
text: Seeing one for the first time can be unsettling.
nxt: It looks like a pale, armored beast the size of a house cat, with segmented plates and large, reflective eyes.

title: Kraken and Colossal Squid
text: Then there are the cephalopods. For centuries, sailors whispered stories of the kraken, a sea monster that could drag wooden ships under the waves.

title: Kraken and Colossal Squid
text: The legends were exaggerated, but the real animals behind them are hardly less astonishing.
nxt: The giant squid and the colossal squid glide through the deep, reaching lengths that can rival a city bus.

title: Kraken and Colossal Squid
text: The giant squid and the colossal squid glide through the deep, reaching lengths that can rival a city bus.
prev: The legends were exaggerated, but the real animals behind them are hardly less astonishing.

title: Kraken and Colossal Squid
text: The colossal squid, living in the freezing waters around Antarctica, has some of the largest eyes in the animal kingdom.

title: Kraken and Colossal Squid
text: A single eye has been measured at about twenty-seven centimeters across, roughly the size of a large dinner plate.
nxt: Why would an animal need an eye like that?

title: Kraken and Colossal Squid
text: Why would an animal need an eye like that?
prev: A single eye has been measured at about twenty-seven centimeters across, roughly the size of a large dinner plate.

title: Kraken and Colossal Squid
text: In a world lit only by faint flickers of bioluminescence, huge eyes help detect the faintest disturbance in the water.

title: Kraken and Colossal Squid
text: Studies of the giant squid suggest that such eyes may help spot something like the distant shadow of a hunting sperm whale.

title: Crabs and Amphipods
text: The pattern keeps going. The Japanese spider crab lurks on the seabed hundreds of meters down.

title: Crabs and Amphipods
text: Its body is only the size of a dinner platter, yet its slender legs stretch nearly four meters from tip to tip,
nxt: like a submerged construction crane tiptoeing over the rocks.

title: Crabs and Amphipods
text: In tide pools, amphipods are tiny crustaceans rarely longer than a few millimeters.
nxt: In deep ocean trenches, researchers have found giant amphipods longer than thirty centimeters.

title: Crabs and Amphipods

title: Crabs and Amphipods
text: Nearby, giant sea spiders with long, spindly legs can span more than half a meter.
nxt: A coastal amphipod is easily swallowed by a minnow, while its abyssal cousin rivals a trout in length.

text: Place these animals beside their coastal cousins and the contrast is impossible to ignore.
nxt: A garden woodlouse fits on your fingertip, while a deep-sea isopod needs two hands.

title: Crabs and Amphipods
text: So what pushes so many unrelated animals toward the same giant destiny?

title: The Clues
text: Down here, the pressure is the first thing you would notice, if you could notice anything at all.
nxt: At sea level, the air presses on your skin with one atmosphere.

title: The Clues
text: Even so, researchers have built several compelling explanations. Let us take them one at a time.

title: Clue One: Cold
text: The first is temperature. Biologists have long observed that warm-blooded animals in cold climates, like polar bears,
nxt: often tend to be larger than their tropical relatives, because a bigger body loses heat more slowly.

title: Slow Growth and Kleiber
text: In near-freezing water, the chemistry of life runs slowly.
nxt: Metabolic rates drop dramatically, and cells may divide at a leisurely pace.

title: Slow Growth and Kleiber
text: Metabolic rates drop dramatically, and cells may divide at a leisurely pace.
prev: In near-freezing water, the chemistry of life runs slowly.
nxt: Isn't it strange how cold water rewires the clock of biology?

title: Slow Growth and Kleiber
text: Isn't it strange how cold water rewires the clock of biology?
prev: Metabolic rates drop dramatically, and cells may divide at a leisurely pace.

title: Slow Growth and Kleiber
text: As a result, some deep-sea creatures are thought to take years to reach maturity.
nxt: With few changes in temperature or light, there may be no deadline to stop growing.

title: Slow Growth and Kleiber
text: With few changes in temperature or light, there may be no deadline to stop growing.
prev: As a result, some deep-sea creatures are thought to take years to reach maturity.

title: Slow Growth and Kleiber
text: Cell by cell, over many quiet years, their bodies keep expanding.

title: Slow Growth and Kleiber
text: That slow growth may work together with a second factor, Kleiber's law.
nxt: It describes how metabolic rate scales with body mass: as an animal gets larger, the energy it needs per gram of tissue goes down.

title: Slow Growth and Kleiber
text: It describes how metabolic rate scales with body mass: as an animal gets larger, the energy it needs per gram of tissue goes down.
prev: That slow growth may work together with a second factor, Kleiber's law.

title: Slow Growth and Kleiber
text: A large body burns fuel more efficiently than a small one, so every calorie counts for more.

title: Slow Growth and Kleiber
text: Think of a large mug of coffee, which stays hot much longer than a tiny espresso cup.
nxt: A small animal has a huge surface area compared to its weight, so it constantly bleeds energy.

title: Slow Growth and Kleiber
text: A tiny shrew must eat almost nonstop. In the deep sea, constant eating is a luxury that does not exist.

title: Marine Snow and Famine
text: There are no kelp forests, no blooming algae, no sunlit reefs. Nearly all food in the abyss comes from the surface far above.

title: Marine Snow and Famine
text: Bits of dead plankton, shed scales and other debris drift downward like a gentle, endless dust. Biologists call it marine snow.

title: Marine Snow and Famine
text: By the time it reaches the seabed, most of its nutrition has already been eaten on the way down.
nxt: What remains is a scattering of crumbs across a watery desert.

title: Marine Snow and Famine
text: What remains is a scattering of crumbs across a watery desert.
prev: By the time it reaches the seabed, most of its nutrition has already been eaten on the way down.

title: Marine Snow and Famine
text: Once in a rare while, a feast arrives, such as the carcass of a whale sinking into the mud.
nxt: But these whale falls can be scattered miles apart and separated by vast stretches of empty time.

title: Marine Snow and Famine
text: But these whale falls can be scattered miles apart and separated by vast stretches of empty time.
prev: Once in a rare while, a feast arrives, such as the carcass of a whale sinking into the mud.

title: Marine Snow and Famine
text: How does an animal survive when meals come months or even years apart?

title: Marine Snow and Famine
text: This is where being big may become a survival strategy. A large body needs less food per gram to keep going.

title: Marine Snow and Famine
text: What if the secret is not how fast you can hunt, but how slowly you can burn?
nxt: Captive giant isopods in aquariums have been reported to live for years without taking a single bite.

title: Marine Snow and Famine
text: Captive giant isopods in aquariums have been reported to live for years without taking a single bite.
prev: What if the secret is not how fast you can hunt, but how slowly you can burn?

title: Marine Snow and Famine
text: Their big bodies may act as living storage tanks. When a meal finally appears, they gorge themselves, then quietly wait out the next famine.

title: Dissolved Oxygen
text: The third factor is dissolved oxygen. Cold water holds gas far better than warm water.

title: Dissolved Oxygen
text: You can see it in your own kitchen, where a warm soda fizzes away while an ice-cold one holds on to its bubbles.

title: Dissolved Oxygen
text: Deep ocean currents begin near the frozen poles, where surface water cools,
nxt: absorbs large amounts of oxygen, becomes dense and sinks.

title: Dissolved Oxygen
text: absorbs large amounts of oxygen, becomes dense and sinks.

title: Dissolved Oxygen
text: It then flows across the globe along the ocean floor, so many abyssal regions contain surprisingly high levels of oxygen.

title: Dissolved Oxygen
text: Why might that matter for size? In Earth's history, high oxygen has sometimes coincided with giants.

title: Dissolved Oxygen
text: In the Carboniferous period, enormous dragonflies and giant millipedes lived on land,
nxt: and some scientists suspect that the oxygen-rich air helped them grow so large.

title: Dissolved Oxygen
text: and some scientists suspect that the oxygen-rich air helped them grow so large.

title: Dissolved Oxygen
text: In a similar way, oxygen-rich cold water may help larger marine animals breathe without extra effort.
nxt: Oxygen does not force animals to grow large, but it may lift the ceiling that would otherwise stop them.

title: Crushing Pressure
text: Yet deep-sea animals are not crushed at all, because their bodies are filled with fluids at the same pressure as the water around them.

title: Crushing Pressure
text: They do not fight the ocean; they exist in harmony with its weight.

title: Crushing Pressure
text: At the molecular level, though, pressure threatens to squash proteins out of shape.
nxt: To survive, deep-sea animals have evolved protective molecules called piezolytes.

title: Crushing Pressure
text: To survive, deep-sea animals have evolved protective molecules called piezolytes.
prev: At the molecular level, though, pressure threatens to squash proteins out of shape.

title: Crushing Pressure
text: One of the best known is TMAO, which binds to water and helps stabilize proteins, like microscopic scaffolding inside every cell.

title: Why Size Helps
text: Size may also bring advantages in a barren world.
nxt: A tiny scavenger is limited to a few square inches of mud, and if no food falls near it, its chances are slim.

title: Why Size Helps
text: A tiny scavenger is limited to a few square inches of mud, and if no food falls near it, its chances are slim.

title: Why Size Helps
text: A giant isopod or amphipod has strong limbs and can cover far more ground, tasting the water for drifting nutrients. Size may also protect.

title: Why Size Helps
text: Some deep-sea predators swallow their meals whole, and past a certain size you simply no longer fit in an enemy's mouth.

title: Giants and Dwarfs
text: Yet nature is never one-dimensional. Right alongside these titans lives the opposite pattern, deep-sea dwarfism.
nxt: Many abyssal snails, clams and small worms tend to be smaller than their shallow-water relatives.

title: Giants and Dwarfs

title: Giants and Dwarfs
text: If being giant is so useful, why doesn't everyone do it?

title: Giants and Dwarfs
text: Because evolution has no single blueprint. Dwarfism is a conservative strategy that cuts the energy needed to build a body to the minimum.

title: Giants and Dwarfs
text: Gigantism is an ambitious one that invests years of slow growth in a long-lasting fortress that can endure a long famine.
nxt: Both paths solve the same riddle in opposite ways.

title: Giants and Dwarfs

title: Strength in Stillness
text: These giants also change what we mean by strength. On our sunlit surface, nature often rewards speed and relentless activity.

title: Strength in Stillness
text: We admire the cheetah's sprint and the falcon's flight, and in our own world we measure success by how quickly we can produce and move on.
nxt: Down in the abyss, survival means stillness and endurance.

title: Strength in Stillness
text: Down in the abyss, survival means stillness and endurance.
prev: We admire the cheetah's sprint and the falcon's flight, and in our own world we measure success by how quickly we can produce and move on.

title: Strength in Stillness
text: The isopod rests on the mud for long stretches. The colossal squid hovers in the gloom, waiting with immense patience for a faint flash of prey.

title: Strength in Stillness
text: Their life is not a sprint against time, but a slow, quiet dance of conservation.

title: Strength in Stillness
text: Can you imagine a place where time seems to stand still? There are no seasons of sunlight, no mornings, no storms.
nxt: The water is as cold and dark today as it was a thousand years ago.

title: Strength in Stillness
text: In that eternal calm, life was free to stretch out, growing at its own pace into shapes of astonishing grandeur.

title: Back to the Surface
text: Now our journey rises toward the surface.
nxt: The pressure eases, the water warms, and faint blue light pierces the ceiling of the sea, brighter with every second.

title: Back to the Surface
text: When you sit at your desk tomorrow, or walk through the quiet evening air, remember the world resting beneath the waves.

title: Back to the Surface
text: While you rush through your day, gigantic animals are resting in darkness miles below,
nxt: breathing freezing water and waiting patiently for the gifts of the sea. Life on Earth does not merely endure the darkness.
